children: Shares of Nvidia fell over 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that the company's board was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid news around his second affair.
The stock shed $14.95 to trade at $158.78, compared with its regular-session closing price of $173.73.

Thesell-off followed a fresh escalation in the leadership crisis after The New York Times reported that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, citing unidentified people who worked at the company. Powell did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The disclosure has left Nvidia's board facing a difficult choice: oust the company's founder and only CEO, who has overseen a more than 700,000% surge in its share price, or retain him amid mounting scrutiny from lawmakers, investors, customers and employees.

Keeping Huang in the role could expose Nvidia to questions over his relationship with Alice Huang and whether it put the company's trade secrets at risk, as well as his reported relationship with an executive who directly reported to him.

The developments have also highlighted Nvidia's lack of a succession plan and how closely the 63-year-old CEO is tied to the company's success. Huang has played a central role in building Nvidia's position in the AI chip market, investing in the AI supply chain and startups, while also acting as one of the industry's most prominent advocates for artificial intelligence.

The latest controversy follows reports concerning Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, who is suspected by US intelligence officials of working for China's Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed, which was spun out of a Chinese gaming enterprise, has been under US investigation for months over potential chip smuggling, Bloomberg reported. Megaspeed and Nvidia have denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed allegations that it spied on Huang.
Nvidia shares had closed 2.92% higher at $173.73 during regular trading on Wednesday before tumbling in extended-hours trade.

title: Nvidia shares sink 8.6% after hours as second affair report puts Jensen Huang's job at risk
